themes.text: PHP's troubles grow with a new unpatched flaw and botnet attacks, Node.js gets its own '2Shell' bug, and supply chain attacks hit shipping and LiteLLM.
A Kona fraud case grows, Roast crowns its 2027 roasters, and electric roasting keeps gaining ground.
The 2027 Tour starts in Edinburgh with 71km of time trials, Lidl-Trek closes its roster, and fall fondos keep rolling.
Holiday fares hit a 10-year high, Delta adds 2027 routes, ETIAS still isn't open, and fall deals run through month-end.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: OpenAI's GPT models arrive on Google Cloud
items.text: GPT-Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are in private preview in Google Cloud's model garden, billed on the Google Cloud invoice. Google says it is now the only hyperscaler offering Gemini, Claude and GPT.

items.head: AI models helped find and exploit the PHP2Shell flaws
items.text: Wiz says Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol helped it find the bugs in August, build working exploits and check the patch. Wiz says every PHP version from the last decade has at least one of the flaws.

items.head: Gemini 4 Argon goes wide at $2/$10, doubling Dec 1
items.text: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to the paid API, AI Studio and Gemini Enterprise. Intro pricing of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens ends Nov 30. Independent rankings are mixed against Claude Opus 5.5.

items.head: AI cloud Modal raises $750 million at a $15.75 billion valuation
items.text: Accel led the Series D. Modal rents GPUs on demand across 13 cloud partners without owning data centers, and says it has passed $1 billion in annualized revenue.

items.head: New unpatched PHP flaw: turn off session upload progress
items.text: PHP disclosed CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution bug with no patch yet. It needs an unusual session configuration, and no exploitation is known. PHP says set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next release.

items.head: Node2Shell: patch Node.js for a CVSS 9.2 Brotli flaw
items.text: CVE-2026-111497 lets crafted compressed data trigger remote code execution in Brotli, affecting Node.js, Bun, Envoy and some Python packages. Proof-of-concept code is out. Update to Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1.

items.head: Mirai botnet joins PHP2Shell attacks as an ASLR bypass appears
items.text: Sophos and Hunt.io tie PHP2Shell traffic to Mirai-style botnets, and VulnCheck built an exploit that works on hardened production setups. No confirmed compromise yet, but Qualys says only 199,000 PHP instances were patched in 12 hours.

items.head: Browsers drop eMudhra certificates after weak CA keys found
items.text: Google, Apple and Microsoft stopped trusting eMudhra SSL/TLS certificates after eight CA keys proved easy to recover. About 30,000 site certificates may need replacing. Python urges pip 26.2.2 or later and fresh containers.

items.head: Supply chain hack lets n0n ransomware into 40+ shipping firms
items.text: Ports and shipping companies in 18 countries were listed by the new n0n group, which demands $1.2 billion in total. CyDome suspects maritime IT vendor CyberLogitec as the entry point; that isn't confirmed.

items.head: Arista patches a VeloCloud SD-WAN Orchestrator zero-day under attack
items.text: CVE-2026-114625, a critical SQL injection, lets any logged-in user gain superuser operator rights. Attacks are ongoing. Update to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 or 6.4.2.12 and limit web access to admin networks.

items.head: Google and Voltus build a 1GW virtual power plant in PJM
items.text: Google is funding a Voltus program that pays businesses and homes to cut use when the grid is strained, growing from 100MW in June. PJM serves 67 million customers in 13 states and DC.

items.head: Microsoft exits a UK AI data center over power delays
items.text: Microsoft pulled out as anchor tenant of Nscale's 50MW Loughton, Essex site after grid officials said power may not arrive until the 2030s. Microsoft says it remains committed to its Nscale partnership.

items.head: Soluna and Applied Digital plan a wind-powered AI site in Texas
items.text: The 50MW Project Dorothy 3 near Silverton in Briscoe County would draw on a 150MW wind farm and the grid. Closing depends on a county tax abatement and is expected by year-end.

items.head: Digital Realty eyes a 1GW campus in Kokomo, Indiana
items.text: The proposed 476-acre site north of Indianapolis would hold three buildings and about 1GW of IT capacity by 2033, with closed-loop cooling. It would be Digital's first in Indiana.

items.head: Tax charges added to the '100% Kona' fraud case
items.text: A superseding indictment brings 28 counts against Kona Coffee Café's owner, who prosecutors say sold foreign coffee as 100% Kona. The government seeks at least $5.26 million; she has pleaded not guilty.

items.head: Roast names its 2027 Roasters of the Year
items.text: Dessert Oasis Coffee Roasters of Ferndale, Michigan, won Micro Roaster of the Year, and Utopian Coffee of Fort Wayne, Indiana, won Macro Roaster of the Year.

items.head: Purebread plans to buy Caffè Artigiano's cafes
items.text: The Canadian bakery chain signed a letter of intent for a C$7.7 million stock deal that would create 27 locations and give Artigiano's owners 49% of Purebread. Not yet final.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.head: NCA Convention, Austin, Texas
items.text: The National Coffee Association's annual convention comes to the JW Marriott Austin.

items.head: 2027 Tour starts in Edinburgh with 71km of time trials
items.text: The 3,479km race runs July 2 to 25, with the most time trial kilometres since 2012 and a queen stage to Col du Portet. Pogačar is chasing a record sixth title.

items.head: Lidl-Trek fills its 2027 roster with Kragh Andersen renewal
items.text: Søren Kragh Andersen signed through 2028, taking the 30th and final spot. Lidl-Trek's eight arrivals include Filippo Ganna and Felix Gall.

items.head: Filippo Ganna leaves Ineos early for Lidl-Trek
items.text: The Italian time trial star signs a three-year deal from 2027, leaving Netcompany-Ineos a year before his contract ended.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: Holiday airfares hit a 10-year high; book by Halloween
items.text: Hopper puts average Thanksgiving tickets near $400, up 31%, and Christmas near $450, up 23%, partly on jet fuel costs. Experts say don't wait for prices to fall.

items.head: Delta adds Boston–Reykjavik for summer 2027
items.text: Daily Boeing 757 flights start April 12 and run seasonally to Oct 30. Delta's previously announced Austin–Paris daily service begins March 27, 2027.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: The EU says the permit is not operational and has no launch date. Over 150 look-alike sites charge €50 to €178; the official fee will be €20.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Use Mobile Passport Control when flying home to DFW or Houston
items.text: US citizens can submit passport details and customs answers in a free app, then show a QR receipt to the CBP officer. Both DFW and IAH take part.
